title: The Mindsets
coreMove: Do not let a first result act like a final label; ask what effort, strategy, help, and time could reveal before you decide what is possible.

exampleSpecs.audience: teachers deciding how to use test data
exampleSpecs.stakes: a student may be tracked away from harder work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Alfred Binet as the anchor for treating a score as a guide to instruction rather than a permanent rank

exampleSpecs.stakes: students may learn to defend rank instead of learn
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast Mrs. Wilson's IQ seating with a classroom routine that removes status from measurement

exampleSpecs.stakes: a developing candidate may be screened out too soon
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Charles Darwin as a reminder that early ordinariness can mislead evaluators

exampleSpecs.domain: adult golf lesson after a public mistake
exampleSpecs.stakes: quitting would preserve pride and stop improvement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Ben Hogan to show that early clumsiness does not settle future skill

exampleSpecs.stakes: one harsh critique could end a developing practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: anchor the response in Cindy Sherman and the fragility of first labels

exampleSpecs.stakes: a poor first read may push the actor into self-protection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Geraldine Page to prevent one awkward audition from becoming an identity label
